notes.title: Small update ea-1.1.0.4 + plans for ea-2
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Fixed Escape button not working when trying to close different windows in the Main Menu
[*] You can now use the Escape key to close the Settings and Profile windows in game
[*] Fixed closing the main window along with secondary popups or windows when using the Escape key
[/list]

Hello everybody! Finally fixed some issues with the Escape button after the ea-1.1 update :D Currently I am still working on an upcoming global update, [b]ea-2[/b]. I may not be as productive as I used to be because of university, but I still try to develop in my spare time. I have some good news, so let's talk about the next update again.

[h3]What is ea-2 all about?[/h3]
This upcoming update fixes one of the main problems - UI navigation. I am redesigning all menus from scratch to allow players to use only their keyboard or controller to navigate the UI, making it possible to play and use different menus without a mouse.

This update also introduces "Online Features" that allow me to dynamically change some small content in the game without having to upload an update to Steam (including different links, tester IDs, etc.). I also added a new "Announcements" section to the main menu. The good thing is that all of this is completely optional and you won't miss out on any game features if you don't have an internet connection.

In this update, I also reworked some core game mechanics and key scripts to make the gameplay smoother and more enjoyable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42643935/b5e9f477fd3768e4c629a5ee34f45a74de6fa852.png[/img]

[h3]When will it be available?[/h3]
It's hard for me to say. But I hope to release the very first preview before 2025. This update will be uploaded to a separate branch, and I will push updates (new previews) to that branch from time to time. I will also post change notes like this for each new preview.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42643935/f0cc1fc06999750a13b8fb4564ee9d48a21466ca.png[/img]

[h3]When will it replace the old version on the main branch?[/h3]
It will take a lot of time to finally replace the old ea-1. There are a lot of things I want to fix and rework after reading some of your feedback. During this development process, you will always be able to switch between the two branches without any conflicts between the two versions of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42643935/3fc915fda7369987097bd73e43bec158c633222e.png[/img]

[h3]Which version should I "main" when ea-2 comes out?[/h3]
The ea-1. Because in the first preview ea-2 will be missing EVERYTHING: the stages and all levels and game modes, the level editor, the profile and so on... It will just be there for you to test if the new stuff and navigation works with your hardware. However, ea2 will slowly recover all the lost features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42643935/02915e6c7d1b25da09467ea2efd4905fe9acbe6a.png[/img]

[h3]Isn't it better to reveal all this stuff when the first preview is released, why now?[/h3]
I just want to be transparent with the players and let you know what I am "cooking" and what to expect :D I will make another post like this when the ea-2 is finally released and it will probably be even more in depth.

Anyway, thanks for reading the announcement! Your feedback and support is always appreciated, so feel free to suggest new ideas in the Community Hub :D Have a nice day!

notes.title: Regular update ea-1.1.0.0
notes.content:
Hello everyone! Back in November 2023 I promised to address some of the Input System and controller issues in the game. So, this update should (sort of) fix most of the bugs.

[h2]New Input System[/h2]
The new version of the game now uses the new Unity Input system alongside the old one. It handles all player inputs in the game and is now responsible for splitting controls between two players in co-op. This means that the game should now support more controllers (although I can't really guarantee this since I only have the Xbox controller that I use to test everything). Also, the co-op experience should now be smoother now, since I couldn't reproduce old bugs that caused controllers or some keyboard keys to break sometimes.

[h2]Localization redone from scratch[/h2]
I have removed all old localization assets in this version. Instead, the game now uses the official Unity localization package. You probably won't notice any changes, but there might be some places, texts and dialogs that I accidentally missed, especially in languages other than English! If you notice any localization issues, be sure to report them.

[h2]Afterword[/h2]
A lot of core mechanics have been reworked in this update, so there may be some issues. If you find a bug, be sure to report it! The new version also uses an updated version of Unity, so as always, if for some reason you are not satisfied with an update, you can go back to ea-1.0 in the [b]Betas[/b] on Steam.

Thank you for supporting the development and have fun! :D

notes.title: The game releases today in Early Access!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! I have some great news for you. Come Together will be available to everyone in Early Access in just a few hours. It has been a really long adventure: lots of devlogs, announcements, events, and a Demo version. But, finally, after all of this, the game will be playable!

[previewyoutube=P7qwNFLKAiw;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Early Access State[/h2]
The game is playable. There are bugs, but they are slowly being fixed. Lots of plans for the next updates, tons of things I want to redo. So stay tuned and report any issues to help with development :D As for content, there are 3 game modes available in Early Access: Main Levels, Flappy Square and Snakether. All the classic levels are completed, you can actually beat the game. The only problem is that there is not much content in them at the moment. But new collectibles, things to buy, secrets, and side quests will be added!

[h2]Level Editor[/h2]
I am actively working on it. But you can already publish your own levels and play what other people have created! I am open to all your ideas and quality of life improvements. Some features are still missing, but they don't make the editor unusable. For example, you can't control the music in custom levels yet.

[h2]Co-Op[/h2]
A lot of influencers and testers have been trying to play co-op. My tests show that it's pretty stable. But sometimes some buttons just refuse to work, especially on non-Xbox controllers. Don't worry about that. Reworking the input system is on my checklist :)

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
It's safe to say that the game is playable and can actually be enjoyed. If you don't mind instabilities or missing features and items here and there, then I guess nothing is stopping you from being a part of the development process :D Our adventure doesn't end here: new game modes with different stages and stories are on the way, tons of other small features are being worked on. I am sure that together we will make a perfect final version!

Thanks to everyone who continues to follow the development and provide feedback. Every contribution is greatly appreciated! Have fun with the game!

notes.title: The biggest Come Together DevLog has arrived!

Hello Come Together testers and players awaiting the game's release! It's the perfect time to post this HUGE devlog covering all the new things and updates that have happened in the last 3 months, as well as the Early Access release date.

[list]
[*] Early Access Release
[*] Level Editor, Custom Levels, and Steam Workshop
[*] New Block Textures (no more empty white blocks)
[*] Shadows
[*] Objects affected by Physics
[*] Stages 4 and 5
[*] New Mechanics: Green Tiles and Deadly Tiles
[*] New Game Mode: Snakether
[*] New Dialogue System with options
[*] Live Menu Background
[*] Mechanics Book and Inventory now work
[*] Co-Op and Controls Split Mode
[*] Custom Cursor
[*] Updated Death and Connection animations
[*] Music switching and new soundtrack
[/list]

[i]These devlogs are a great way to keep the public informed about the current state of development, they help game testers understand what has been changed and what might need their attention. Most importantly, they give you a much better idea of what the game is all about. Thank you and have a nice day![/i]
